questions.q: What is the SI unit of electric current?
questions.explanation: The ampere is the SI base unit of electric current.

questions.q: What is the dimensional formula of velocity?
questions.explanation: Velocity = length/time = LT⁻¹.

questions.q: What is the dimensional formula of linear momentum?
questions.explanation: Momentum = mass × velocity = M × LT⁻¹ = MLT⁻¹.

questions.q: A screw gauge has a pitch of 1 mm and 100 divisions on its circular scale. What is its least count?
questions.explanation: Least count = pitch / number of circular divisions = 1/100 = 0.01 mm.

questions.q: Which of the following physical quantities can be added to a quantity with dimensions ML²T⁻²?
questions.explanation: Only quantities with the same dimensions can be added; torque has dimensions ML²T⁻², like energy.

questions.q: In a pendulum experiment g = 4π²l/T². The length is l = 100.0 cm with an error of 0.1 cm, and the period is T = 2.00 s with an error of 0.02 s. What is the percentage error in g?
Express a speed of 54 km/h in m s⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Multiplying km/h by 5/18 gives m s⁻¹.

questions.q: Stokes' law gives the viscous force on a sphere as F = 6πηrv. Use this to find the dimensional formula of the coefficient of viscosity η.
questions.explanation: The numerical factor 6π is dimensionless, so only F, r and v matter.

questions.q: A runner completes one full lap of a circular track and returns to the starting point. His displacement is
questions.explanation: Displacement is the straight-line change in position, which is zero when he ends where he began.

questions.q: The slope of a velocity–time graph gives
questions.explanation: Slope of v–t graph = dv/dt = acceleration.

questions.q: A car starts from rest with a uniform acceleration of 3 m s⁻². What is its speed after 6 s?
An object is dropped from rest. Taking g = 9.8 m s⁻², how far does it fall in 2 s?
A ball is thrown vertically upward at 20 m s⁻¹ (g = 10 m s⁻²). What is its average speed over the first 4 s of motion?
questions.explanation: It rises 20 m in 2 s and falls 20 m in the next 2 s, so the distance is 40 m and the average speed is 40/4 = 10 m s⁻¹ (average velocity is zero).

questions.q: Two cars 500 m apart approach each other along a straight road at constant speeds of 20 m s⁻¹ and 30 m s⁻¹. After how long do they meet?
questions.explanation: Relative speed = 50 m s⁻¹, so time = 500/50 = 10 s.

questions.q: A stone is dropped from a height of 80 m (g = 10 m s⁻²). Find the time it takes to reach the ground and its speed on impact.
questions.explanation: Free fall from rest: h = ½gt² and v = gt.

questions.q: A driver travelling at 20 m s⁻¹ sees an obstacle and applies the brakes after a reaction time of 0.5 s. The car then decelerates uniformly at 5 m s⁻². Find the total distance travelled from the moment the obstacle is seen until the car stops.
questions.explanation: The car moves at constant speed during the reaction time and then decelerates uniformly.

questions.q: In uniform circular motion, the acceleration of the body is directed
questions.explanation: Centripetal acceleration points along the radius towards the centre.

questions.q: The scalar product of two perpendicular vectors is
questions.explanation: A · B = AB cos 90° = 0.

questions.q: What is the horizontal component of a velocity of 20 m s⁻¹ directed 60° above the horizontal?
A particle moves on a circle of radius 2 m with a speed of 4π m s⁻¹. What is its time period?
A projectile is launched at 20 m s⁻¹ at 60° to the horizontal. What is its speed at the highest point of its path?
questions.explanation: Only the horizontal component remains at the top: 20 cos 60° = 10 m s⁻¹.

questions.q: Rain falls vertically at 10 m s⁻¹. A man walks on a level road at 10 m s⁻¹. At what angle to the vertical should he tilt his umbrella to keep dry?
options: 45°, tilted forward (in the direction he walks)
questions.explanation: Relative to the man the rain has a horizontal component of 10 m s⁻¹ towards him and a vertical one of 10 m s⁻¹, so it comes from 45° ahead of him.

questions.q: Find the horizontal range of a projectile launched at 20 m s⁻¹ at an angle of 45° (g = 10 m s⁻², level ground).
questions.explanation: At 45° the range is u²/g = 40 m.

questions.q: A ball is struck at 30 m s⁻¹ at 30° above the horizontal (g = 10 m s⁻², level ground, no air resistance). Find the maximum height and the horizontal range.
questions.explanation: Apply the standard formulae with sin 30° = 0.5 and sin 60° = 0.866.

questions.q: One newton is equal to
questions.explanation: F = ma, so 1 N = 1 kg × 1 m s⁻².

questions.q: The force of friction between two surfaces acts
options: opposite to the relative motion (or its tendency)
questions.explanation: Friction opposes the relative motion, or the tendency of relative motion, between the surfaces.

questions.q: What is the momentum of a 2 kg body moving at 5 m s⁻¹?
questions.explanation: p = mv = 2 × 5 = 10 kg m s⁻¹.

questions.q: A 5 kg block rests on a table. A string attached to it pulls it vertically upward with a force of 20 N (the block stays on the table). Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the normal force from the table?

A 4 kg block on a smooth horizontal table is connected by a light string over a smooth pulley at the table edge to a 1 kg block hanging freely. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the acceleration of the system?
questions.explanation: a = m₂g/(m₁ + m₂) = 10/5 = 2 m s⁻².

questions.q: A frictionless road is banked so that a car can negotiate a bend of radius 40 m at 20 m s⁻¹ without any friction. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the angle of banking?
A 2000 kg truck is acted on by a net force of 5000 N. Find its acceleration and the speed it reaches from rest after 4 s.
questions.answer: Acceleration = 2.5 m s⁻²; speed after 4 s = 10 m s⁻¹.
questions.explanation: Use Newton's second law and then v = u + at with u = 0.

questions.q: A 2 kg block rests on top of a 4 kg block that lies on a smooth floor. The coefficient of friction between the blocks is 0.3. What is the maximum horizontal force that can be applied to the lower block so that the upper block does not slip? (g = 10 m s⁻².)
keyPoints: Maximum acceleration of the upper block = μg = 3 m s⁻²
Both blocks must share this acceleration
questions.explanation: Friction on the upper block can supply at most μmg, limiting the common acceleration to μg.

questions.q: The work done by a force is zero when the force is
questions.explanation: W = Fs cosθ is zero when θ = 90°.

questions.q: One joule is the same as one
questions.explanation: Work = force × distance, so 1 J = 1 N m.

questions.q: If the speed of a body is doubled, its kinetic energy becomes
questions.explanation: KE ∝ v², so doubling v multiplies KE by 4.

questions.q: A 60 kg person climbs a staircase of vertical height 10 m in 20 s. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the average power used against gravity?
questions.explanation: Work = mgh = 6000 J; power = 6000/20 = 300 W.

questions.q: A 0.5 kg pendulum bob on a 1 m string is released from the horizontal position. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is its speed at the lowest point?
questions.explanation: It falls 1 m, so v = √(2gl) = √20 ≈ 4.5 m s⁻¹.

questions.q: A 0.5 kg block moving at 4 m s⁻¹ on a smooth surface hits a spring of force constant 200 N m⁻¹ and compresses it until it stops. What is the maximum compression?
A ball dropped from a height of 4 m rebounds to a height of 1 m. Find the coefficient of restitution.
questions.explanation: e is the ratio of the speed after to the speed before the collision.

questions.q: A train engine delivers a constant power of 20 kW while the train moves at a constant speed of 20 m s⁻¹. Find the resistive force acting on the train.
keyPoints: At constant speed, driving force = resistive force
questions.explanation: With zero acceleration the driving force equals the resistance, and P = Fv.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: What is the SI unit of the moment of inertia?
questions.explanation: I = Σmr², so its unit is kg m².

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: The angular momentum of a system is conserved when
options: the net external force is zero
the net external torque is zero
questions.explanation: Since τ = dL/dt, L is constant when the net external torque vanishes.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A solid sphere of mass 5 kg and radius 0.2 m has a moment of inertia (about a diameter) of ⅖MR². What is its value?

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A wheel of radius 0.5 m rotates at 10 rad s⁻¹. What is the linear speed of a point on its rim?

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A solid disc rolls without slipping on a horizontal surface. What fraction of its total kinetic energy is rotational?
questions.explanation: Rotational KE = ½ × ½MR² × (v/R)² = Mv²/4; total = 3Mv²/4; the fraction is 1/3.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A uniform horizontal beam of mass 10 kg and length 4 m is hinged at one end and supported at the other end. Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what force does the support exert?
questions.explanation: Taking torques about the hinge: F × 4 = 100 × 2, so F = 50 N.

questions.topic: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.q: A particle of mass 2 kg moves in a circle of radius 0.5 m at a speed of 4 m s⁻¹. Find its angular momentum about the centre.
keyPoints: L = m v r (velocity is perpendicular to radius)
questions.explanation: For circular motion, L = mvr.

questions.q: The value of the acceleration due to gravity at the Earth's surface is approximately
questions.explanation: Near the Earth's surface g ≈ 9.8 m s⁻².

questions.q: The universal law of gravitation was proposed by
questions.explanation: Isaac Newton stated that every particle attracts every other with a force proportional to the product of the masses and inversely proportional to the square of the distance.

questions.q: If the distance between two masses is doubled, the gravitational force between them becomes
questions.explanation: F ∝ 1/r², so doubling r divides F by 4.

questions.q: What is the acceleration due to gravity at a height equal to twice the Earth's radius above the surface?
questions.explanation: The distance from the centre is 3R, so g' = g R²/(3R)² = g/9.

questions.q: For a satellite in a circular orbit, what is the ratio of its kinetic energy to the magnitude of its gravitational potential energy?
questions.explanation: KE = GMm/2r and |PE| = GMm/r, so the ratio is 1/2.

questions.q: Taking g = 10 m s⁻² and the Earth's radius as 6400 km, what is the approximate period of a satellite orbiting just above the Earth's surface?
The acceleration due to gravity on the Moon is 1.6 m s⁻². What would a 60 kg person weigh on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Mass is the same everywhere; only the weight changes with local g.

questions.q: Hooke's law holds good within the
questions.explanation: Stress is proportional to strain only within the elastic limit.

questions.q: The ratio of tensile stress to tensile strain is called
questions.explanation: This ratio is Young's modulus.

questions.q: A force of 100 N is applied uniformly over a cross-section of 2 cm². What is the stress?
questions.explanation: Stress = 100/(2 × 10⁻⁴ m²) = 5 × 10⁵ Pa.

questions.q: A wire is subjected to a stress of 4 × 10⁸ Pa and shows a strain of 0.002. What is its Young's modulus?
questions.explanation: Y = stress/strain = 4 × 10⁸/0.002 = 2 × 10¹¹ Pa.

questions.q: A wire of length 2 m, cross-section 1 mm² and Young's modulus 2 × 10¹¹ Pa behaves like a spring. What is its force constant k = YA/L?
A wire of force constant k is cut into two equal halves. What is the force constant of each half?
questions.explanation: k = YA/L, so halving L doubles k.

questions.q: Why are steel cables, rather than rubber ropes, used in cranes to lift heavy loads?
questions.answer: Steel has a much larger Young's modulus than rubber, so it stretches very little under a heavy load and stays within its elastic limit.
keyPoints: Steel has a high Young's modulus
Small strain for a given stress
Remains within elastic limit and is strong
questions.explanation: A larger Young's modulus means less extension for the same stress.

questions.q: Bernoulli's principle is based on the conservation of
questions.explanation: Bernoulli's equation is an expression of energy conservation for a flowing ideal fluid.

questions.q: In streamline (steady) flow of a fluid
options: the velocity at any given point remains constant with time
the velocity changes irregularly at every point
the fluid rotates about every point
questions.explanation: In steady flow every fluid particle passing a given point has the same velocity.

questions.q: A wooden block of volume 2 × 10⁻³ m³ is held completely under water (density 1000 kg m⁻³). Taking g = 10 m s⁻², what is the buoyant force?
questions.explanation: Buoyant force = ρVg = 1000 × 2 × 10⁻³ × 10 = 20 N.

questions.q: The pistons of a hydraulic press have areas of 10 cm² and 1000 cm². What force must be applied on the small piston to lift a weight of 1000 N on the large piston?

According to Poiseuille's formula, the volume flow rate of a viscous liquid through a tube is proportional to r⁴ (for fixed pressure difference, length and liquid). If the radius is doubled, the flow rate becomes
questions.explanation: Flow rate ∝ r⁴, so 2⁴ = 16 times.

questions.q: The height to which a liquid rises in a capillary tube is inversely proportional to the radius of the tube. If a tube of half the radius is used, the height of the rise
questions.explanation: h = 2S cosθ/(rρg) ∝ 1/r, so halving r doubles h.

questions.q: Why do small drops of mercury on a smooth surface take an almost spherical shape?
questions.answer: Because of surface tension: a liquid surface tends to have the least possible area, and a sphere has the smallest surface area for a given volume.
keyPoints: Surface tension tends to minimise surface area
A sphere has minimum surface area for a given volume
Gravity is negligible for very small drops
questions.explanation: Minimising surface energy leads to a spherical shape.

questions.q: Water flows steadily through a pipe of radius 2 cm at a speed of 1 m s⁻¹. The pipe narrows to a radius of 1 cm. Find the speed in the narrow section and the volume flow rate.
questions.answer: Speed = 4 m s⁻¹; volume flow rate ≈ 1.26 × 10⁻³ m³ s⁻¹.
questions.explanation: The flow rate Av is the same in every section.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of specific heat capacity?
questions.explanation: c = Q/(mΔT), with unit J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹.

questions.q: An ideal black body is one that
options: reflects all radiation falling on it
transmits all radiation falling on it
absorbs none of the radiation falling on it
absorbs all radiation falling on it
questions.explanation: A perfect black body absorbs all incident radiation (and is also the best emitter).

questions.q: A thermometer reads 98.6 °F. What is this in degrees Celsius?
How much heat is needed to melt 2 kg of ice at 0 °C? (L = 3.36 × 10⁵ J kg⁻¹.)
A bimetallic strip made of two metals with different coefficients of linear expansion is heated. What happens?
options: It bends, with the metal of larger expansion coefficient on the outer (convex) side
It bends, with the metal of larger expansion coefficient on the inner (concave) side
It expands only along its length
questions.explanation: The metal that expands more becomes longer, so it lies on the outside of the curve.

questions.q: Two rods of equal length and cross-section are joined end to end. Rod A has thermal conductivity 2k and rod B has k. The free end of A is held at 100 °C and the free end of B at 0 °C. What is the steady-state temperature at the junction?
questions.explanation: Equal heat flow: 2k(100 − T) = k(T − 0), so 200 = 3T and T = 66.7 °C.

questions.q: A 1 kW heater is used to heat 0.5 kg of water from 20 °C to 100 °C. Taking c = 4200 J kg⁻¹ K⁻¹ and ignoring losses, find the time required.
questions.explanation: Energy supplied by the heater equals the heat absorbed by the water.

questions.q: A process that takes place at constant pressure is called
questions.explanation: 'Isobaric' means constant pressure.

questions.q: The internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on its
questions.explanation: An ideal gas has no intermolecular potential energy, so U depends only on T.

questions.q: What is the efficiency of a Carnot engine operating between a source at 500 K and a sink at 400 K?
A gas is compressed at a constant pressure of 1 × 10⁵ Pa from 3 litres to 1 litre (1 litre = 10⁻³ m³). What is the work involved?
questions.explanation: |W| = PΔV = 10⁵ × 2 × 10⁻³ = 200 J; since the volume decreases, the work is done on the gas.

questions.q: A diatomic ideal gas (γ = 1.4) is compressed adiabatically to half its volume. By what factor does its pressure increase? (Use 2^1.4 ≈ 2.64.)
questions.explanation: PV^γ is constant, so P₂/P₁ = (V₁/V₂)^γ = 2^1.4 ≈ 2.64.

questions.q: A heat engine of efficiency 30% does 600 J of work per cycle. How much heat does it reject to the sink per cycle?
questions.explanation: Heat absorbed = 600/0.3 = 2000 J; heat rejected = 2000 − 600 = 1400 J.

questions.q: State the first law of thermodynamics and write its mathematical form.
questions.answer: The heat supplied to a system equals the increase in its internal energy plus the work done by the system: Q = ΔU + W.
keyPoints: It is a statement of energy conservation
Q = heat supplied, ΔU = change in internal energy, W = work done by the system
questions.explanation: Heat supplied is shared between raising internal energy and doing work.

questions.q: According to classical kinetic theory, the kinetic energy of the molecules of an ideal gas at absolute zero is
questions.explanation: KE ∝ T, so it would vanish at T = 0.

questions.q: The value of the universal gas constant R is about
questions.explanation: R ≈ 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (while 1.38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹ is the Boltzmann constant).

questions.q: How many molecules are there in 2 g of hydrogen gas (H₂, molar mass 2 g mol⁻¹)?
questions.explanation: 2 g of H₂ is one mole, which contains 6.022 × 10²³ molecules.

questions.q: At constant temperature the volume of a fixed mass of an ideal gas is halved. Its pressure
questions.explanation: By Boyle's law PV is constant, so halving V doubles P.

questions.q: A container holds 2 mol of gas A and 3 mol of gas B at a total pressure of 5 atm (ideal gases, no reaction). What is the partial pressure of A?
questions.explanation: Partial pressure = mole fraction × total pressure = (2/5) × 5 = 2 atm.

questions.q: What is the ratio of the rms speed of the molecules of a gas at 400 K to that at 100 K?
questions.explanation: v_rms ∝ √T, so the ratio is √(400/100) = 2.

questions.q: How many molecules are there in 1 litre of an ideal gas at STP? (Molar volume at STP = 22.4 L, N_A = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.)
questions.explanation: Divide Avogadro's number by the molar volume in litres.

questions.q: The restoring force acting on a particle in simple harmonic motion is given by
questions.explanation: In SHM the restoring force is proportional to displacement and opposite to it.

questions.q: For small oscillations, the time period of a simple pendulum depends on
options: its length and the acceleration due to gravity
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(l/g) depends on l and g only.

questions.q: A particle performs SHM with amplitude 5 cm. What total distance does it cover in one complete oscillation?
questions.explanation: In one oscillation it covers 4 amplitudes: 4 × 5 = 20 cm.

questions.q: A spring of force constant 50 N m⁻¹ is stretched by 0.2 m. How much elastic potential energy is stored?
A particle in SHM has angular frequency 2 rad s⁻¹ and amplitude 0.5 m. What is its speed when its displacement is 0.3 m?
Two simple pendulums have lengths 1 m and 4 m. What is the ratio of their time periods?
Why does the amplitude of a real oscillating pendulum gradually decrease with time?
questions.answer: Because of damping: air resistance and friction at the support dissipate the pendulum's mechanical energy as heat.
keyPoints: Mechanical energy is gradually lost as heat
questions.explanation: The energy of an oscillator is proportional to the square of its amplitude, so energy loss reduces the amplitude.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of frequency?
questions.explanation: Frequency is measured in hertz (1 Hz = 1 s⁻¹).

questions.q: The audible range of frequencies for a normal human ear is approximately
questions.explanation: Humans typically hear from about 20 Hz to 20 kHz.

questions.q: A wave is described by y = A sin(kx − ωt) with k = π/2 m⁻¹. What is its wavelength?
The speed of sound in a gas is proportional to the square root of its absolute temperature. If the absolute temperature is made four times, the speed of sound becomes
questions.explanation: v ∝ √T, so quadrupling T doubles v.

questions.q: Two waves of amplitudes 3 units and 1 unit superpose to produce beats. What is the ratio of the maximum to the minimum intensity?
questions.explanation: Maximum amplitude = 4, minimum = 2; intensity ∝ amplitude², so the ratio is 16 : 4 = 4 : 1.

questions.q: A string 0.6 m long is fixed at both ends and the wave speed on it is 120 m s⁻¹. What is the frequency of its third harmonic?
questions.explanation: Fundamental f₁ = v/2L = 120/1.2 = 100 Hz; the third harmonic is 3 × 100 = 300 Hz.

questions.q: A ship's sonar sends an ultrasonic pulse down and receives the echo from the sea bed 0.2 s later. If the speed of sound in sea water is 1500 m s⁻¹, find the depth of the water.
questions.explanation: The pulse travels to the sea bed and back, so the depth is half the total path.
